scope: Primary papers and official runtime documentation; mechanisms and applicability, not a comprehensive survey or performance reproduction

sources.evidence: Profiles progress when jobs share a GPU and keeps or reverses packing according to observed benefit.
sources.adaptation: Use actual co-run progress to validate busy-based candidate hints.
sources.limit: Its time slicing, migration and cluster mechanisms are not our existing process runtime.

sources.evidence: Scheduling uses attained service with unknown or partial duration information and promotes waiting jobs.
sources.adaptation: Track historical work and waiting debt; retain starvation reservations.
sources.limit: Our nonpreemptive policy does not inherit Tiresias's preemptive scheduling behavior.

sources.evidence: Uses finish-time fairness relative to an isolated-share reference and auctions among disadvantaged applications.
sources.adaptation: Measure service shortfall and individual harm, using an explicitly different service-debt heuristic.
sources.limit: No auction, finish-time fairness theorem, or multi-GPU reference is reproduced.

sources.locator: Sections 3.1 (effective throughput and space sharing), 3.2, 4.1 and 4.3
sources.evidence: Models throughput under resource allocations, including distinct rates for colocated combinations.
sources.adaptation: Normalize each job by its same-configuration solo rate and use exact-group measurements.
sources.limit: A single-GPU incremental heuristic does not implement its cluster allocation optimizer.

sources.evidence: A consolidated execution service provides iteration scheduling, fast switching and memory sharing.
sources.adaptation: Treat fast preemption as a separate runtime capability, not a free policy option.
sources.limit: TensorFlow execution-service primitives are not automatically available to separate PyTorch processes.

sources.evidence: Accounts for dynamic training throughput and user-defined adaptation schedules in fairness and efficiency planning.
sources.adaptation: Version measurements by phase and approved training configuration; refresh stale evidence.
sources.limit: V2 does not implement its market equilibrium or stochastic dynamic programming.

sources.locator: Progressive MCGS and Appendix G examples (version 1 inspected)
sources.evidence: Cross-branch evolution can combine backbones, losses and preprocessing.
sources.adaptation: Treat full candidate pipelines and all lineage sources as context.
sources.limit: Local implementation audit takes precedence; paper examples do not quantify our mutation distribution.

sources.evidence: Search operators draft, debug and improve executable ML solutions.
sources.adaptation: Track actual mutations, not just stage labels.
sources.limit: A related agent architecture, not a scheduler or our local code.

sources.locator: Method: model retrieval, refinement and ensembling
sources.evidence: Refines pipeline components and combines solutions.
sources.adaptation: Represent component plans and pipeline changes.
sources.limit: Does not provide GPU interference guarantees.

sources.evidence: Brief new-application/dataset profiling is combined with past observations and refreshed on behavior changes.
sources.adaptation: Use historical priors plus current-candidate measurements.
sources.limit: Cluster findings and profiling machinery are not reproduced.

sources.locator: Abstract and tile-level prediction method; ASPLOS 2025
sources.evidence: Composes tile-level predictions to forecast unseen-model/hardware latency.
sources.adaptation: Prefer operator/tensor descriptors over a family name.
sources.limit: Solo performance generalization is not co-run generalization.

sources.evidence: Uses iterative labeled graph neighborhoods for efficient graph comparison.
sources.adaptation: Directed typed neighborhood histogram as a lossy structural descriptor.
sources.limit: Not an isomorphism proof or performance metric; our distance is an adaptation.

sources.system: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
sources.evidence: Adapts uncertainty sets to changing distributions.
sources.adaptation: Monitor calibration under drift, keeping per-target uncertainty separate from distance.
sources.limit: No conformal method is implemented; long-run coverage is not per-job safety.

sources.locator: API contract / Understanding CUDA Memory Usage
sources.evidence: The fraction limits the caching allocator and raises allocator OOM when exceeded.
sources.adaptation: State the limits of guarded solo calibration.
sources.limit: Allocator limiting and live telemetry do not guarantee a whole-process VRAM ceiling.

sources.locator: API contract / Understanding CUDA Memory Usage
sources.evidence: Direct CUDA or third-party allocations can exist outside the PyTorch allocator.
sources.adaptation: State the limits of guarded solo calibration.
sources.limit: Allocator limiting and live telemetry do not guarantee a whole-process VRAM ceiling.
